public_rationale: The current-state components have strong support. February reporting quotes an OpenAI executive confirming that Code Red had not ended, and independent testing establishes Google as a close competitor. The earlier conventional-wisdom component is less secure. Contemporary coverage described OpenAI as dominant, but also discussed credible rivals and an uncertain lead. That does not establish how widely people regarded its position as unassailable. Scoring the whole statement supported would require treating dominance as equivalent to a difficult-to-challenge lead. The evidence also does not justify declaring that earlier perception false.
limitations: The Code Red source is original news reporting presented in an AI-translated English edition; it warns that translated quotations may differ from the original wording.
Benchmark comparisons establish competitive capabilities, not equality in adoption or commercial position.
Several potentially useful contemporary pages could not be read and were excluded.
The reputational component depends on an imprecise period and an unspecified population of commentators.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: A couple of years ago the conventional wisdom was that OpenAI was unassailable, but now, by its own account, OpenAI is in a Code Red, with Google right on its heels.

statement.excerpt: It is important to remember that a couple years ago the conventional wisdom (which I long cast doubt on here) was that OpenAI was unassailable. Now, by their own lights, they are in a Code Red, with Google right on their heels.
statement.document_title: Does OpenAI’s new financing make sense?

from_speaker: they are in a Code Red
our_interpretation: This is a comparison between OpenAI's reputation roughly in 2023–2024 and its competitive position at publication on 2026-02-27. The target interval encompasses both parts; evidence must address the appropriate part.
For the ongoing state described by 'now', use February 2026 through the post date, the latest publicly reportable period before publication.

Read 'unassailable' as widely perceived to have a commanding lead that would be difficult to challenge. Neither literal invulnerability nor unanimous agreement is required, but evidence of leadership alone is insufficient.
Read 'Code Red' as an internally declared competitive emergency still current at publication.
Read 'right on their heels' as Google being a close competitor in frontier model capabilities. Marcus supplies no benchmark or numerical threshold.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous coverage establishes a widespread earlier perception of a difficult-to-challenge OpenAI lead; OpenAI statements or reliable reporting establish a current Code Red; and contemporary capability comparisons establish Google as a close competitor.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable evidence establishes that Code Red had ended before publication, that Google remained substantially behind across relevant capabilities, or that the alleged earlier conventional wisdom materially misrepresents contemporary views. Distinct supported and contradicted components would warrant mixed.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning 'However, the company has not lifted the code red'
evidence.explanation: The report identifies Kim as OpenAI Korea head Kim Kyung-hoon and attributes confirmation of the continuing Code Red to him. This supports the February status through an executive's reported account; no public internal memo was obtained.

evidence.excerpt: The 6 evaluations that Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview leads
evidence.locator: Paragraph immediately before 'CritPt Benchmark Leaderboard - Results (18 Feb '26)'
evidence.explanation: The dated evaluation places Gemini 3.1 Pro at the top of the overall index, supporting Google as a close frontier competitor. The same report places it behind GPT-5.2 on GDPval-AA, so it does not establish superiority on every task.

evidence.excerpt: but it is still early in the game.
evidence.explanation: This establishes contemporary recognition of OpenAI's dominance. The article also discusses credible challengers and conditional expectations, so dominance alone does not establish a conventional belief in an unassailable position.

evidence.locator: Section 'Who will win out?', opening sentence
evidence.explanation: The article treats OpenAI and Anthropic as having a head start and includes Google's Gemini among the leading models. This is material evidence against treating the entire 2023–2024 period as an uncontested consensus, but one article cannot disprove a broadly held earlier perception.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A broader, dated set of contemporary industry assessments establishing whether belief in a difficult-to-challenge OpenAI lead was widespread during the earlier period, together with direct confirmation of Code Red's status at publication.
